name: Eric Larchevêque
current_role: Manager (gérant) and largest shareholder of TBSO (listed AI/fintech group); co-founder and former CEO/chairman of Ledger
profile: French serial entrepreneur since 1996 (Montorgueil, Prixing). Founded La Maison du Bitcoin in Paris, which merged with BTChip and Chronocoin in 2014 to form Ledger, the hardware crypto-wallet maker he led as CEO until 2019. Now an angel investor, TV investor on M6, and head of TBSO, which in 2026 dropped a bitcoin-treasury plan to build an AI/fintech group.
interesting_fact: Ledger was born in Vierzon (Cher), and in 2019 he co-founded ALGOSUP, a five-year software-development school, in the same town with Franck Jeanin.
deep_cut_fact: As an investor on M6's 'Qui veut être mon associé ?' he committed €590,000 in season 1, the third-largest total of the panel; he trained as an engineer at ESIEE Paris (MSc in information-processing architecture).
notes: Very public in French media and podcasts; best route is likely via TBSO investor relations or the M6 show/press. No published personal contact found in this pass. Recent interview: https://www.toutsurmesfinances.com/actualites/?p=799

name: Mike McCue
profile: American tech entrepreneur who never attended college: founded Paper Software (sold to Netscape for $20M in 1996), co-founded voice-browser Tellme Networks (acquired by Microsoft in 2007), then co-founded the Flipboard news-magazine app in 2010, which he still leads and has pushed into the open social web/fediverse.
interesting_fact: He gave up a congressional nomination to the US Air Force Academy to support his family after his father died, joined IBM on a six-month temp contract in 1986 and stayed three and a half years.
deep_cut_fact: His Netscape project to turn Navigator into a web-based desktop OS was codenamed 'Constellation' after a boat his father helped restore; he later bought a 48-foot classic wooden sailboat and named it Constellation too. His first app was a space-shuttle flight simulator written in TI-BASIC in 1981.
notes: Media-friendly; frequent podcast guest on the open social web. Press contact is the 'Contact Us' link on Flipboard's press page.

name: Ety Spiegel Hubara
current_role: Co-founder, Orca Security (listed on org charts as Head of SRE)
profile: Israeli engineer and one of eight co-founders of Orca Security, the agentless cloud-security platform founded in 2019 (largely by ex-Check Point colleagues) and valued at about $1.8B in 2021. She has kept a low public profile, working on the site-reliability/engineering side rather than as a company spokesperson.
interesting_fact: Orca Security was founded by eight co-founders and reached unicorn status within about two years, joining the Israeli unicorn club in late 2020/2021.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Orca's About page publishes a general info@orca.security address; better route may be via CEO Gil Geron or Orca PR.

name: Tim Trefren
current_role: Working on climate at Recheck (identity/compliance platform for US residential solar; reported as co-founder & CEO)
profile: Co-founded product-analytics company Mixpanel with Suhail Doshi in Y Combinator's Summer 2009 batch and worked there 2009-2019 (latterly VP of Customer Success); Mixpanel hit a $1.05B valuation in 2021. He now works on climate through Recheck, a Hanover, NH-based identity, compliance and reputation layer for the residential solar industry.
interesting_fact: Recheck says it has 50,000+ verified solar sales reps and that partners account for 90%+ of US residential solar financing - a natural fit for an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Recheck's founding team is drawn from Mixpanel, HipChat, Notarize and Ohm Analytics, and the company is based in Hanover, New Hampshire rather than Silicon Valley.
notes: YC's Mixpanel page says he is 'now working on climate change at Recheck'; his exact title (CEO) comes from aggregator sites, so confirm. Strong energy-podcast angle (residential solar trust/compliance).

name: Olugbenga Agboola
profile: Nigerian fintech founder ('GB') who co-founded Flutterwave with Iyinoluwa Aboyeji in 2016 and became CEO in 2018. Flutterwave builds pan-African payments infrastructure, raised a $250M Series D at a $3B+ valuation in 2022, holds licences in 34+ African countries, acquired open-banking firm Mono in 2026 and in April 2026 won a Nigerian microlender licence.
interesting_fact: Before Flutterwave he worked at PayPal, Google (on the Wallet payments product), Royal Bank of Scotland, Standard Bank Nigeria and Sterling Bank; he holds an MIT Sloan MBA.
deep_cut_fact: Besides an MIT MBA he holds a master's in behavioural engineering and IT security plus EC-Council IT-security certifications; in 2024 he was named vice chair of the US Chamber of Commerce's US-Africa Business Center board.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Milken, Money20/20, US Chamber events) - speaker bureaus/event organisers are a viable route. No published press email confirmed in this pass. Vice-chair info from Wikipedia Flutterwave article.

name: Samir Vasavada
current_role: Co-founder and Co-Head of Vise (New York)
profile: Co-founded Vise in 2016 with Runik Mehrotra while both were teenagers; Vise is an SEC-registered AI investment platform that builds, manages and explains personalised portfolios (direct indexing, models, tax-loss harvesting) for financial advisers. It reached a $1B valuation in 2021; Vasavada now co-heads the company from NYC.
interesting_fact: Flatiron Health founders Nat Turner and Zach Weinberg wrote Vise's first $100K check, and Founders Fund co-led its $2M seed.
deep_cut_fact: Vise's origin story: when Runik went to UPenn, Samir moved onto his dorm floor and refused to leave until Runik dropped out; Runik's parents agreed only if they first raised $1M - which they did.
notes: Team page lists him as 'Co-Head of Vise' alongside co-founder Runik Mehrotra. No published press email found; vise.com/press page is the media entry point.
